This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies.\n\n## Look up the account first\n- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.\n- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.\n\n## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit\nA charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.\n\n| Situation | What Support does |\n|---|---|\n| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line within Support's limit | Issue one credit note with reason `duplicate` for the full amount of the duplicated line, against that line. No handoff is needed. Tell the customer the amount credited. |\n| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line over the limit | Don't credit. Open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. |\n| Duplicate the console doesn't confirm (different request IDs, or no second line) | Don't credit. Collect the intake details and hand the case to Billing Ops as the routing page describes. |\n\nSupport's limit is set by Finance in the Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive) (the duplicate-charge credit row). It is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits.\n\n## What Support never credits\n- Goodwill, exceptions, SLA credits, or any credit someone says a manager, sales rep or Redwood engineer already approved. These stay with Finance, per the #support guidance from FP&A. Route the request; don't issue anything from the console.\n- Marketplace purchases, which are billed by the marketplace.\n\n## Telling the customer\n- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. It replaces the v0.3 billing escalations RACI draft in the customer-success shared drive, which predates the Billing Ops and Billing Engineering rotations and should not be used.\n\n## When a case is needed\nOpen a case only when the customer asks for something Support can't do in the conversation, or reports a problem the related pages don't explain. Answering a question needs no case.\n\n- Answer, don't hand off: how billed tokens are counted (model-native tokenizer, full request payload), why retries and cancelled streams are billed, and why the Console lags a few minutes are covered in the related pages. If one of them explains what the customer sees, explain it and stop there, even if the customer calls it a bug or double billing.\n- If an older page says something different from the current one, explain the current behaviour and which page is current. That needs no case, even if the customer asks to report the old page as a bug.\n- Questions about typical credit amounts, with no credit asked for, get the answer that there is no standard amount and that any amount is decided in Finance's review. No case.\n- Ask for the intake details before handing off. The receiving team works from the case and the conversation so far, so put everything the customer gave you in the case.\n- If the customer doesn't have some of the details, hand off with what you have and note what's missing. Don't hold the case until they find them.\n\n## Routing table\n| Case | Owning team | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Disputed or duplicated line on a direct Redwood invoice | Billing Ops | Invoice number, the line(s), UTC window, request IDs |\n| Refund request on a direct invoice line the customer says was billed in error | Billing Ops | Billing Ops confirms the charge and requests approval where needed |\n| Invoice total doesn't match the customer's usage export | Billing Ops | Note the export's timezone and filters |\n| Payment failures, holds, receipts | Billing Ops | |\n| Meter discrepancy the related pages don't explain: request IDs whose billed tokens still don't match after the tokenizer, payload and retry rules are applied | Billing Engineering | Billing Eng checks meter correctness and hands any correction to Billing Ops |\n| Request for a credit, goodwill credit, waiver, or removal of charges that were billed correctly (including retries), or an exception to a billing rule | Finance | The ask, the amount if given, and why. Applies even when Support has just explained that the charge is correct |\n| SLA credit request on a self-serve account | Finance | Self-serve plans have no SLA; tell the customer, and still route the request. If the customer says a contract covers them, use the next row instead |\n| SLA credit claim on an account with a signed contract | Account team | The CSM/TAM checks the contract's SLA terms and files the claim with Finance |\n| Customer says they have a contract the console doesn't show | Account team | The account team confirms the contract and owns any request that depends on it, including an SLA credit. Treat the account as the console shows it until then |\n| Usage for successful (2xx) requests still missing from the Console after about 30 minutes | Telemetry | A pipeline issue, not a billing one; see the onboarding triage playbook |\n\n## Not owned by Billing Ops\n- Credit, goodwill and exception requests go to Finance, per FP&A's guidance in #support (June 2025). Billing Ops only applies adjustments that have been approved.\n- Questions about what a customer's contract or SLA says go to the account team, per the same #support guidance. Answer the general rule and tell the customer their account team confirms their terms; don't quote a figure from the contract. A request to confirm a contract figure, such as a discount rate, needs no case: tell the customer their account team confirms it. Open an account team case only for an SLA credit claim under the contract.\n\n## What not to do\n- Don't route a billing case to SRE unless there is an active incident.\n- Don't route credit or exception requests to Legal; Finance pulls Legal in when needed.\n- Don't promise an outcome, amount, or timeline when you hand off.\n- Don't share credit percentages or typical ranges with customers, including the SLA credit table in the incident closure procedure. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01AUPQdpebvBKeZjueKDPFeA","type":"tool_result","content":"===== support-process/token-accounting-discrepancy-intake-and-triage.json\ntitle : Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)\nspace : customer-success-and-support\nauthor : Naomi Feldman\nowner_team : customer-success\nstatus : published\ncreated_at : 2024-11-19\nlast_updated : 2025-04-22\nreviewers : ['Ava Chen', 'Dev Patel']\nlabels : ['billing', 'token-accounting', 'support-process', 'triage']\nrelated_pages : ['confluence://customer-success-and-support/support-process/customer-intake-channels', 'confluence://product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/billing-meters-v3']\nconfidentiality : internal\n[body]\n## Purpose\nThis page documents how Support should handle and count reports of a **token accounting discrepancy** across intake channels. These cases frequently arrive via Slack, email, or Jira, and can be double-counted unless we normalize to a single canonical support record.\n\n## Definition (use this phrase)\nWe classify a case as a *token accounting discrepancy* when a customer claims that billed token totals (Console Usage and/or invoice export) do not match their own calculation from application logs or local tokenization.\n\n## Approved intake channels\nWe track where the report first arrived, because it affects response time and deduplication.\n- Jira (customer-support): SUP-* ticket created directly by Support\n- Slack: #support threads (often started from Intercom/Zendesk summaries)\n- Gmail: finance/billing or CSM forwards to leadership/finance\n\n## How to avoid double counting\n1. If a report arrives in Slack or Gmail, file a SUP ticket and link it.\n2. Mark the SUP ticket label `token-accounting` and add the origin channel in the description (Slack/Gmail).\n3. In weekly reporting, count the case by *origin* (Slack vs Gmail vs Jira), not by total artifacts.\n\n## Common root causes to check\n- Streaming retries/reconnect (tokens can be emitted twice)\n- Client counts only final chunk tokens\n- Different tokenizer / unicode normalization\n- Whitespace/newlines included in input strings\n- Tool-call serialization adds tokens\n- Prefix-cache billing bug (rare; see SUP-3009)\n\n## Known examples (for reference)\n- SUP-2841: streaming retry/reconnect behavior leading to perceived token accounting discrepancy\n- SUP-2917: embeddings tokenizer mismatch leading to perceived token accounting discrepancy\n- SUP-3009: cache-hit + tool calling bug leading to real token accounting discrepancy\n\n## Reporting note\nWhen answering: \"Which intake channel has the most reports of token accounting discrepancy?\" be sure to include Slack and Gmail-origin cases even if a SUP ticket was created later.\n===== known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation.json\ntitle : Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation\nspace : customer-success-and-support\nauthor : Aisha Rahman\nowner_team : customer-success\nstatus : published\ncreated_at : 2025-02-14\nlast_updated : 2025-02-18\nreviewers : ['Priya Natarajan', 'Dev Patel', 'Ben Carter']\nlabels : ['usage', 'billing', 'tokens', 'streaming', 'retries', 'workaround']\nconfidentiality : internal\nrelated_pages : ['customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook', 'eng-platform/runbooks/usage-pipeline']\n[content]\n## Overview\nSome customers reconcile Redwood token usage against internal estimates and may observe higher usage totals. The most common causes are (1) client retries and (2) streaming cancellation behavior.\n\nThis page provides a support-ready explanation and recommended mitigations.\n\n## Key definitions\n- **Attempt**: a single request admitted by the Redwood API gateway (server-side).\n- **Logical request**: what the customer thinks of as one user action; may map to multiple attempts if the client retries.\n\n## What we bill\n### Retries\n- Redwood usage is recorded per-attempt.\n- If a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each admitted attempt can be billable.\n- The Usage dashboard lists rows by **request_id** (attempt identifier).\n\n### Streaming cancellation\n- **Prompt tokens** are counted once the request is admitted (even if the client cancels the stream later).\n- **Completion tokens** are counted based on tokens actually generated/streamed prior to cancellation.\n\n## Common customer symptoms\n- We only sent N requests but we see >N rows: retries created additional attempts.\n- We timed out at 15s so we expected zero bill: prompt tokens + partial completion tokens may still be counted.\n\n## Recommended mitigations\n1) Avoid automatic retries on client-side timeouts for long generations.\n2) Increase client timeout where possible (align to max expected generation time).\n3) Reduce max_tokens / output length to meet latency budgets.\n4) For troubleshooting, ask for a small set of request_ids + the customers retry/cancel metrics.\n\n## Support playbook (quick response blurb)\nWe record usage per server-admitted attempt. If your client retries after a timeout, each admitted attempt can appear separately in Usage and can be billable. confluence://product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-first-production-launch-prd\n - confluence://architecture-and-standards/api-standards/onboarding-event-schema-v1\n - confluence://eng-platform/how-tos/checklist-progress-service-integration\n - confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/onboarding-kpis-dashboard-spec\n - confluence://security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/onboarding-telemetry-data-review\n - confluence://product-docs/release-notes/console-guided-onboarding-checklist-2025-04\n[body]\n## Purpose\nThis playbook standardizes how Support and Customer Success (CS) triage onboarding issues for Redwood Hosted API customers using the **Console onboarding checklist** (\"Guided onboarding\" + \"First production launch\" checklist).\n\nIt covers:\n- How to interpret checklist state (what it means, what it does *not* mean)\n- Standard intake questions and what evidence to collect\n- Common onboarding failures and recommended fixes\n- When and how to escalate to Console, Platform, Telemetry, SDK, or SRE\n\nNon-goals:\n- This is not a full troubleshooting guide for all API issues.\n- This does not cover Dedicated/Private onboarding beyond basic pointers.\n\n---\n\n## Audience and assumptions\n**Primary users:** Support Engineers, CS Engineers, On-call CS.\n\nAssumptions:\n- Customer is using **Hosted API** (unless explicitly noted).\n- Support has access to Redwood Console support views and internal tooling.\n- Support can view high-level request metadata (status codes, timestamps, region) but should avoid requesting sensitive data.\n\n---\n\n## Quick definitions\n**Checklist**: A set of steps surfaced in Console with completion state stored in the Checklist Progress Service.\n\n**Step state**:\n- **Not started**: We have not observed the completion signal.\n- **In progress**: Partial signals observed (e.g., API key created but no successful request yet).\n- **Complete**: Completion event(s) observed and accepted.\n- **Blocked / needs attention** (UI label): Customer likely hit a common failure mode; the system may surface guidance.\n\n**Important:** Checklist state is computed from events. A customer can be “working correctly” even if a step is incomplete due to telemetry delay or missing instrumentation.\n\n**TTFS / TTFP**:\n- **TTFS (Time to First Success)**: time from signup to first successful (2xx) API response for an eligible endpoint.\n- **TTFP (Time to First Production)**: time from signup to first sustained production traffic (as defined in the metrics spec).\n\n---\n\n## Where to find checklist state (Support workflow)\n1) Open the customer’s **Console tenant**.\n2) Navigate to: **Onboarding → Checklist** (or the checklist card on the Console home page).\n3) If available, open **Support View** (shows timestamps and event source metadata).\n4) If the customer is on a call, confirm they are looking at the **same tenant/workspace** (many issues are “wrong org/workspace”).\n\nWhat to capture in the ticket:\n- Tenant/workspace ID\n- Checklist step names + states (screenshot or copy/paste)\n- Timestamp of last observed checklist update\n- Customer-reported time of last attempted action (e.g., “sent request 10 minutes ago”)\n\n---\n\n## Interpreting checklist state: do’s and don’ts\n### Do\n- Use the checklist as a **structured interview**: it narrows the likely failure mode.\n- Cross-check with request metadata: recent status codes, request counts, regions.\n- Treat steps as **signals**, not as ground truth.\n\n### Don’t\n- Don’t ask for customer prompts, full payloads, or raw logs unless required and approved.\n- Don’t mark steps complete manually unless (a) you’ve validated success via internal signals or (b) you are unblocking a UI issue and leaving an audit note.\n\n---\n\n## Standard intake questions (ask in this order)\nUse these as macros in tickets and live troubleshooting.\n\n### A) Account / project alignment\n1. Which **workspace/tenant** are you using? (Ask for org/workspace name as shown in Console.)\n2. Which **API key** are you using (name/label, not the full secret)? When was it created?\n3. Where are you setting the key (env var name, secret manager, CI/CD)?\n\n### B) Request details (minimal)\n4. Which SDK/language and version are you using? (e.g., Python SDK vX.Y, TS SDK vX.Y, OpenAI-compat)\n5. Which endpoint are you calling? (chat, completions, embeddings)\n6. Region/edge: which base URL/region are you targeting?\n7. What error are you seeing (status code + error message string)?\n\n### C) Production readiness context\n8. Are you testing streaming? If yes, what client environment (browser/node/server) and how are you consuming the stream?\n9. Have you configured retries/timeouts?\n10. Are you seeing 429s? If yes: expected request rate and concurrency.\n\n---\n\n## Common failures mapped to checklist steps\nThe table below maps top onboarding ticket categories to likely checklist step states and fixes.\n\n| Symptom / Ticket theme | Likely checklist step(s) | Fast diagnosis | Recommended fix | Escalate when |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 401/403 “Invalid API key” / auth failure | “Create API key” complete but “First successful request” not complete | Wrong workspace, wrong env var name, using revoked key, OpenAI-compat key header mismatch | Verify tenant, re-create key, ensure correct env var, confirm header format per SDK | If correct key still fails with consistent 403 across regions (Platform/Auth) |\n| First request “works” but checklist doesn’t update | “First successful request” not complete | Telemetry delay, request routed via non-instrumented path, tenant mismatch | Wait 5–10 minutes; confirm request hit Hosted gateway; verify correct org | If >30 minutes delay with verified 2xx requests (Telemetry) |\n| Streaming disconnect confusion / partial output | “Streaming response” incomplete or flagged | Client not reading stream properly, idle timeout, missing reconnect logic | Use SDK streaming helper; ensure keep-alive; implement reconnect/backoff | If consistent disconnect at same server timestamp across customers/regions (SRE/Platform) |\n| Immediate 429 after launch | “Quotas & rate limits” incomplete or flagged | Concurrency too high, burst traffic, missing backoff | Configure backoff + retry; adjust quotas; recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput | If 429s occur well below configured quota or inconsistent quota enforcement (Platform/Metering) |\n| Usage dashboard mismatch / “requests aren’t counted” | “View usage dashboard” incomplete/flagged | Dashboard freshness delay, wrong time range/filters, multiple orgs | Explain freshness window; check usage dataset lag; confirm correct filters | If freshness SLA breached or lag spikes (Telemetry/Data Eng) |\n| Model changes / unexpected behavior post-launch | “Pin model version” incomplete | Using floating alias, not pinned version, mismatch between environments | Pin model version; Confirm customer is in the expected workspace.\n2. Confirm they are using a currently active key (not deleted/rotated).\n3. Verify the environment variable name used in docs for their SDK.\n4. For OpenAI-compat usage: confirm base URL and auth header naming per our compatibility layer.\n\nEscalation criteria:\n- Multiple customers reporting 401/403 with newly created keys in the same hour.\n- Auth failures occur across multiple keys and workspaces with no configuration mistakes.\n\nEscalate to: **Platform/Auth** (Kaitlyn Nguyen) and **SRE** if widespread.\n\n### 2) First successful API call (TTFS)\n**What completion means:** We observed the first eligible 2xx response from the Hosted gateway for the tenant.\n\nTroubleshooting:\n1. Ask for a timestamp of their last attempt.\n2. Check internal request metadata for 2xx vs 4xx/5xx.\n3. If they are using a local proxy, confirm requests actually reach Hosted.\n4. Confirm the quota limits visible in Console.\n2. Ask for peak RPS and concurrency.\n3. Check whether 429s align with bursts.\n4. Ensure they have backoff configured.\n\nEscalation criteria:\n- 429 occurs below configured quota or quota changes not applying.\n\nEscalate to: **Metering/Quotas** (Cole Summers) and **Telemetry** if enforcement vs reporting mismatch.\n\n### 6) Usage dashboard and billing alignment\n**What completion means:** They visited usage dashboards; does not guarantee they understand freshness windows.\n\nKey guidance to provide:\n- Usage dashboards are near-real-time but can lag (communicate current freshness SLA displayed in Console).\n- Ensure correct workspace, time range, and environment filters.\n\nEscalation criteria:\n- Freshness lag exceeds SLA or discrepancy persists beyond normal windows.\n\nEscalate to: **Telemetry/Data Eng** (Mei Lin) with screenshots and timestamps.\n\n### 7) Model pinning and fallback policy (first production launch)\n**What completion means:** They pinned a model version and configured a fallback policy.\n\nTriage prompts:\n- Are they using a floating alias?\n- Did they configure fallback across regions or to a compatible model variant?\n- Are they seeing unexpected model IDs in responses?\n\nEscalation criteria:\n- Control plane displays correct config but gateway routes differently.\n\nEscalate to: **Control Plane/Config** (Ethan Park / Benji Okafor).\n\n---\n\n## Escalation routing and required evidence\n### Severity guidance (Support)\n- **Sev 1 (Production down):** Customer cannot serve production traffic due to a Redwood-side issue (widespread or confirmed service degradation). Engage SRE immediately.\n- **Sev 2 (Major impact):** Customer blocked from launching / significant traffic impaired; workaround not available.\n- **Sev 3 (Standard onboarding issue):** Misconfiguration, docs confusion, or expected limits.\n\n### Escalation checklist (include in ticket)\nWhen escalating, include:\n- Tenant/workspace ID\n- Region(s)\n- Approx timestamps (UTC) of failures/successes\n- Endpoint (chat/embeddings/etc.)\n- Status codes distribution (e.g., 401 vs 429 vs 5xx)\n- Checklist step states + last update time\n- SDK/language + version\n- Whether issue reproduces across keys and environments\n\n### Team routing\n- **Console checklist UI issues (missing card, broken deep links, step drawer bugs):** Console team (Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin). Provide browser + Console build version.\n- **Checklist state wrong / delayed / inconsistent:** Telemetry + Checklist Progress Service owners (Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman). Provide event timestamps and any evidence of out-of-order behavior.\n- **Auth/API key problems:** Platform/Auth (Kaitlyn Nguyen). Provide key creation time and error strings.\n- **Quota enforcement vs UI mismatch:** Metering/Quotas (Cole Summers) + Telemetry.\n- **Routing/model pinning/fallback issues:** Control Plane/Config (Ethan Park / Benji Okafor).\n- **Widespread errors / suspected incident:** SRE on-call (Sean Gallagher’s org). Provide region and error rates.\n\n---\n\n## Admin override: when to use and how to document\nSupport can use admin override tools to mark steps complete/reset **only** in the following cases:\n- **UI is blocking the customer** (e.g., checklist gating a UI panel) and Support has verified the underlying action succeeded by other signals.\n- **Telemetry gap** prevents a correct completion state and the customer needs to proceed immediately.\n- **Customer requests a reset** for training/demo purposes (rare; ensure it’s the correct tenant and authorized).\n\nRules:\n- Always add an audit note with: reason, evidence source, and the customer contact.\n- Do not use override to “hide” genuine failures.\n\nSuggested audit note template:\n- Reason:\n- Evidence (timestamp, request metadata, screenshot, etc.):\n- Action taken (mark complete / reset):\n- Support agent:\n\nEscalate before overriding if:\n- You suspect a systemic telemetry regression.\n- Overrides are needed repeatedly for multiple customers.\n\n---\n\n## Data handling and privacy\n- Do not request or store customer prompts, full request bodies, or model outputs in Support tickets unless explicitly approved for that case.\n- Collect only metadata necessary to debug (timestamps, status codes, tenant ID, SDK version).\n- Checklist and onboarding telemetry are designed to be **PII-free**; if you observe PII in an event payload or UI surface, treat as a potential security issue and escalate to Security (Marcus Lin) immediately.\n\n---\n\n## Appendix A: Known limitations (as of April 2025 release)\n- Checklist completion can lag behind real actions due to ingestion delays.\n- Some integrations (older SDKs, custom gateways) may not emit client hint tags; server-side events should still cover core steps.\n- Out-of-order event arrival has been observed in dogfood; race-condition fixes are in place, but anomalies may persist in edge cases.\n\n---\n\n## Appendix B: Support macros (copy/paste)\n### Macro: Request minimal debugging info\n“Can you share (1) workspace/org name as shown in Console, (2) which SDK/language + version, (3) the endpoint you’re calling, and (4) the status code + error message text? confluence://product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-first-production-launch-prd\n - confluence://architecture-and-standards/api-standards/onboarding-event-schema-v1\n - confluence://eng-platform/how-tos/checklist-progress-service-integration\n - confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/onboarding-kpis-dashboard-spec\n - confluence://security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/onboarding-telemetry-data-review\n - confluence://product-docs/release-notes/console-guided-onboarding-checklist-2025-04\n[body]\n## Purpose\nThis playbook standardizes how Support and Customer Success (CS) triage onboarding issues for Redwood Hosted API customers using the **Console onboarding checklist** (\"Guided onboarding\" + \"First production launch\" checklist).\n\nIt covers:\n- How to interpret checklist state (what it means, what it does *not* mean)\n- Standard intake questions and what evidence to collect\n- Common onboarding failures and recommended fixes\n- When and how to escalate to Console, Platform, Telemetry, SDK, or SRE\n\nNon-goals:\n- This is not a full troubleshooting guide for all API issues.\n- This does not cover Dedicated/Private onboarding beyond basic pointers.\n\n---\n\n## Audience and assumptions\n**Primary users:** Support Engineers, CS Engineers, On-call CS.\n\nAssumptions:\n- Customer is using **Hosted API** (unless explicitly noted).\n- Support has access to Redwood Console support views and internal tooling.\n- Support can view high-level request metadata (status codes, timestamps, region) but should avoid requesting sensitive data.\n\n---\n\n## Quick definitions\n**Checklist**: A set of steps surfaced in Console with completion state stored in the Checklist Progress Service.\n\n**Step state**:\n- **Not started**: We have not observed the completion signal.\n- **In progress**: Partial signals observed (e.g., API key created but no successful request yet).\n- **Complete**: Completion event(s) observed and accepted.\n- **Blocked / needs attention** (UI label): Customer likely hit a common failure mode; the system may surface guidance.\n\n**Important:** Checklist state is computed from events. A customer can be “working correctly” even if a step is incomplete due to telemetry delay or missing instrumentation.\n\n**TTFS / TTFP**:\n- **TTFS (Time to First Success)**: time from signup to first successful (2xx) API response for an eligible endpoint.\n- **TTFP (Time to First Production)**: time from signup to first sustained production traffic (as defined in the metrics spec).\n\n---\n\n## Where to find checklist state (Support workflow)\n1) Open the customer’s **Console tenant**.\n2) Navigate to: **Onboarding → Checklist** (or the checklist card on the Console home page).\n3) If available, open **Support View** (shows timestamps and event source metadata).\n4) If the customer is on a call, confirm they are looking at the **same tenant/workspace** (many issues are “wrong org/workspace”).\n\nWhat to capture in the ticket:\n- Tenant/workspace ID\n- Checklist step names + states (screenshot or copy/paste)\n- Timestamp of last observed checklist update\n- Customer-reported time of last attempted action (e.g., “sent request 10 minutes ago”)\n\n---\n\n## Interpreting checklist state: do’s and don’ts\n### Do\n- Use the checklist as a **structured interview**: it narrows the likely failure mode.\n- Cross-check with request metadata: recent status codes, request counts, regions.\n- Treat steps as **signals**, not as ground truth.\n\n### Don’t\n- Don’t ask for customer prompts, full payloads, or raw logs unless required and approved.\n- Don’t mark steps complete manually unless (a) you’ve validated success via internal signals or (b) you are unblocking a UI issue and leaving an audit note.\n\n---\n\n## Standard intake questions (ask in this order)\nUse these as macros in tickets and live troubleshooting.\n\n### A) Account / project alignment\n1. Which **workspace/tenant** are you using? (Ask for org/workspace name as shown in Console.)\n2. Which **API key** are you using (name/label, not the full secret)? When was it created?\n3. Where are you setting the key (env var name, secret manager, CI/CD)?\n\n### B) Request details (minimal)\n4. Which SDK/language and version are you using? (e.g., Python SDK vX.Y, TS SDK vX.Y, OpenAI-compat)\n5. Which endpoint are you calling? (chat, completions, embeddings)\n6. Region/edge: which base URL/region are you targeting?\n7. What error are you seeing (status code + error message string)?\n\n### C) Production readiness context\n8. Are you testing streaming? If yes, what client environment (browser/node/server) and how are you consuming the stream?\n9. Have you configured retries/timeouts?\n10. Are you seeing 429s? If yes: expected request rate and concurrency.\n\n---\n\n## Common failures mapped to checklist steps\nThe table below maps top onboarding ticket categories to likely checklist step states and fixes.\n\n| Symptom / Ticket theme | Likely checklist step(s) | Fast diagnosis | Recommended fix | Escalate when |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 401/403 “Invalid API key” / auth failure | “Create API key” complete but “First successful request” not complete | Wrong workspace, wrong env var name, using revoked key, OpenAI-compat key header mismatch | Verify tenant, re-create key, ensure correct env var, confirm header format per SDK | If correct key still fails with consistent 403 across regions (Platform/Auth) |\n| First request “works” but checklist doesn’t update | “First successful request” not complete | Telemetry delay, request routed via non-instrumented path, tenant mismatch | Wait 5–10 minutes; confirm request hit Hosted gateway; verify correct org | If >30 minutes delay with verified 2xx requests (Telemetry) |\n| Streaming disconnect confusion / partial output | “Streaming response” incomplete or flagged | Client not reading stream properly, idle timeout, missing reconnect logic | Use SDK streaming helper; ensure keep-alive; implement reconnect/backoff | If consistent disconnect at same server timestamp across customers/regions (SRE/Platform) |\n| Immediate 429 after launch | “Quotas & rate limits” incomplete or flagged | Concurrency too high, burst traffic, missing backoff | Configure backoff + retry; adjust quotas; recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput | If 429s occur well below configured quota or inconsistent quota enforcement (Platform/Metering) |\n| Usage dashboard mismatch / “requests aren’t counted” | “View usage dashboard” incomplete/flagged | Dashboard freshness delay, wrong time range/filters, multiple orgs | Explain freshness window; check usage dataset lag; confirm correct filters | If freshness SLA breached or lag spikes (Telemetry/Data Eng) |\n| Model changes / unexpected behavior post-launch | “Pin model version” incomplete | Using floating alias, not pinned version, mismatch between environments | Pin model version; set fallback policy | If pinned version still routes unexpectedly (Control Plane) |\n| Retrying causes duplicate side effects | “Retries & timeouts” incomplete | Non-idempotent operations, missing idempotency keys | Add idempotency keys and safe retry policy | If SDK helper seems broken or headers dropped (SDK team) |\n\n---\n\n## Step-by-step triage by checklist section\n### 1) API key creation & environment setup\n**What completion means:** An API key was created in Console (or via admin provisioning).\n\nTroubleshooting:\n1. Confirm customer is in the expected workspace.\n2. Confirm they are using a currently active key (not deleted/rotated).\n3. Verify the environment variable name used in docs for their SDK.\n4.
